analysis.evidence: אֶת marks הָעֹרֵב, “the raven,” as the object Noah sends out. The next verb, וַיֵּצֵא, “and it went out,” describes the raven’s response.
analysis.morphology: Piel wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and no suffix

analysis.evidence: In וַיְשַׁלַּח אֶת הָעֹרֵב, “he sent out the raven,” אֶת introduces הָעֹרֵב, the definite noun naming what he sent out.
analysis.morphology: Direct-object marker without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיְשַׁלַּח אֶת הָעֹרֵב, אֶת marks the raven as the object of “he sent out.” The raven then goes out and back until the waters dry up.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a masculine singular absolute common noun.

analysis.evidence: Noah sends the raven, and the raven is the subject of וַיֵּצֵא. The following infinitives יָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב describe its repeated going out and returning.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third-person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־
analysis.sense: go out, depart from a place or someone’s presence

analysis.evidence: יָצוֹא repeats the preceding finite verb וַיֵּצֵא, “it went out.” Paired with וָשׁוֹב, “and returning,” it describes the raven repeatedly going out and coming back until the waters dried up.
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive absolute, without prefix or suffix
analysis.sense: go out, depart from a place or someone’s presence

analysis.evidence: The raven is the subject of וַיֵּצֵא. The paired infinitives יָצוֹא וָשׁוֹב describe its repeated movement out and back until the waters dried up.
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive absolute with prefixed conjunction וָ־
analysis.sense: return to one’s place of origin

analysis.evidence: עַד יְבֹשֶׁת הַמַּיִם marks the drying up of the waters as the endpoint of the raven’s going to and fro.
analysis.morphology: Preposition without prefix or suffix, governing the infinitive construct יְבֹשֶׁת.

analysis.evidence: In עַד יְבֹשֶׁת הַמַּיִם מֵעַל הָאָרֶץ, הַמַּיִם is the subject of the infinitive. The phrase gives the endpoint of the raven’s going to and fro: “until the waters dried up from the surface of the earth.”
analysis.morphology: Qal infinitive construct with a final ־ת, governed by עַד.

analysis.evidence: In יְבֹשֶׁת הַמַּיִם מֵעַל הָאָרֶץ, עַל locates the waters on the surface of the earth, and מֵ־ marks the surface from which they dry up.
analysis.morphology: Preposition עַל with prefixed מֵ־ (from מִן, “from”).

analysis.evidence: In הַמַּיִם מֵעַל הָאָרֶץ, מֵעַל means “from upon.” The ground is the surface the floodwaters covered until they dried up.
analysis.morphology: Definite article הָ־ prefixed to a common noun, singular absolute.
